paragraphs: The GLE500e was part of the first-generation GLE (W166) range from 2016 to 2018. It uses the M276 — a 3.0-litre V6 petrol engine — paired with an electric motor, making it a plug-in hybrid (PHEV). The GLE500e was discontinued in 2018, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLE500E on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the GLE500E from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The GLE500e's M276 engine has specific PHEV-related components and integration that set it apart from a standard M276. Fitting a non-PHEV engine or assuming standard parts will work can cause issues with the hybrid system and ECU. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your vehicle is a GLE500e with the PHEV system - The specific M276 variant fitted to your model year - The condition of the electric motor and associated ancillaries - Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build
